title: Cardiology Language Access: A Clinical Workflow
summary: A practical cardiology language access workflow for symptom history, tests, medications, consent, discharge, and telecardiology.
body_markdown:
###


Cardiac care crosses symptom triage, tests, procedures, medication changes, discharge, and rehabilitation. A specialty workflow assigns language support at each handoff and protects details such as timing, dosage, and warning signs.


###


Preserve the patient’s own words for the sensation, location, onset, duration, pattern, triggers, associated symptoms, and change over time. Do not replace the description with a diagnosis.


###


Healthcare-specific AI interpretation with appropriate controls can be a first-line option in many workflows. Human interpreters remain complementary according to patient preference, organizational policy, and encounter needs.


###


Prioritize the medication schedule, specified warning signs, who to contact, the next appointment, and any activity, monitoring, or site-care instructions. The patient should explain the plan in their own words.


###


Confirm language before the visit, send understandable join steps, start interpretation before clinical discussion, identify every speaker, and keep a fallback channel. Document the language and modality used.
